requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: Stops the MessagePack analyzer from crashing on certain invalid contracts. In TypeCollector, when a member's key kind (int or string) differs from the other members, the member is now skipped after the MsgPack005 diagnostic is reported. Before, the code went on to dereference a null key. Duplicate int and string keys are no longer added to the member dictionaries a second time, so Dictionary.Add no longer throws. The same guards are applied to the field loop, but only for mixed key kinds and duplicate int keys. The change adds analyzer tests showing diagnostics are reported for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, execution tests for run-time round-tripping, and a README section.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stops working for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types since 3.1.1. The diff's theory is that the analyzer was throwing inside TypeCollector on duplicate or mixed keys. The diff does not touch any code that decides whether suppressed types are analyzed at all. So it is not shown that this is the root cause of the reported regression rather than a related crash. The new tests MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported are the real evidence for that.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents which analyzer rules do and do not apply to suppressed types.
The duplicate-key crash guard also changes behavior for normal (generated) types, covered by DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes.
An execution test project file checks run-time serialization of a suppressed type, which is not analyzer behavior.

Medium that this is the actual fix for the regression; the diff shows no change to suppression handling, so it relies on the tests passing. Low for the field-loop changes: no test uses fields, and the field string-key add after line 1170 is not visible. README claims about MsgPack012 are not tested.

findings.description: The field-loop string-key branch continues past the visible hunk, and its stringMembers.Add is not shown as guarded. Duplicate string keys on fields may still throw and crash the analyzer. No test uses fields with duplicate or mixed keys, so the C4/C5 field-loop guards are also untested.

The diff only adds crash guards and does not touch suppression handling. It is not shown that a duplicate or mixed-key crash is what made the analyzer silent for SuppressSourceGeneration types since 3.1.1. Whether the regression is fixed depends on MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported actually failing before this change.

`continue` skips all later per-member processing for a mismatched key member, including formatter-attribute handling and any later per-member diagnostics such as MsgPack003. Those diagnostics may no longer appear for that member.

SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed only asserts that there are no diagnostics. It would also pass if the analyzer skipped suppressed types entirely, which is the bug, so it does not by itself guard the fix.
README states that MsgPack012 (accessibility) is reported for suppressed types, but no test covers it.

In the field loop's string-key else branch (beginning at lines 1168-1170), stringMembers.Add was not guarded with !stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey), unlike the property loop (lines 1039-1042) and both intMembers.Add branches (lines 1023-1026 and 1163-1166). If two fields have the same string [Key], or a field duplicates a property's string [Key], stringMembers.Add will still throw ArgumentException after reporting MsgPack005 and crash the analyzer. None of the new duplicate-key tests cover fields.
